reader.title: Lynching of Frank Lang'y
bases: The only report says the people of the section 'went in a body', took the captured man from the officers and hanged him to a tree (A1).

A1 reports that a crowd ('in a body') took an accused murderer and cattle thief from officers and hanged him, which meets the definition, but it is a single unsourced brief in a distant Dakota paper with no date, place or corroboration (A1).
Only one brief, in the Turner County Herald, reports the event, and no second account was found (A1).

summary.text: The lynching of Frank Lang'y was the hanging, in Oklahoma in about May or June 1888, of a man described as an outlaw, after local people took him from the officers who held him.
It is known from a single brief in the Turner County Herald of Hurley, Dakota, which gave no date beyond 'recently' and no place more exact than Oklahoma.
The Herald described Frank Lang'y, also called James, as 'a noted outlaw and desperado' who had murdered half a dozen people and stolen hundreds of head of cattle.
These accusations appear in the brief as the paper's own statements, with no source named and no mention of any charge or trial.
According to the brief, a posse captured him and placed him in the charge of officers.
As soon as the people of that section learned of the capture, they 'went in a body, took him from the officers in charge and hanged him to a tree.'
The item names none of the lynchers or officers, gives no number for the crowd, and does not state the victim's race.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

The Turner County Herald ran the story on 14 June 1888 as one paragraph in 'Doings in the South', a column of regional briefs that also carried a suspected child murder in Missouri, an embezzlement in Memphis and a hotel fire in Texas.
The paper offered no comment on the hanging and repeated the accusations against the dead man as fact.
No other account of the hanging appears in the coverage.

accounts.label: Regional news brief
accounts.gist: An outlaw captured by a posse in Oklahoma was taken from the officers by the people of the section, who went in a body, and hanged to a tree.

framing.detail: The Turner County Herald ran the item without comment among unrelated crime and disaster briefs, repeating the accusations as fact ('who has murdered half a dozen people').
